name: teamwork-tasks-from-desk
description: Turn a Teamwork.com Desk ticket into a structured Teamwork.com Projects task (plus optional subtasks) without leaving the terminal. User provides a Desk ticket URL (https://<workspace>.teamwork.com/desk/tickets/<id>); plugin fetches the ticket — subject, customer, chronological message thread (replies + internal notes) and email attachments — via the Teamwork Desk REST API (https://apidocs.teamwork.com/docs/desk), asks for a Teamwork Projects URL (project or tasklist) so it knows where to file the work, and for an assignee email (may be empty for unassigned). When the proposed task naturally splits into multiple roles (BE/FE/QA/migration), the plugin asks for an email per role. The assignee is resolved via GET /projects/api/v3/people.json?searchTerm=<email>. Using the WAME canonical task format ([preamble] → HR → ## Akceptačné kritériá → HR → ## Cieľ → HR → ## Technický popis) the plugin synthesises a draft main task — title, description, optional subtasks, per-task estimate (WAME senior + Claude Code methodology, 15-minute step, 480-minute cap, split-proposal above 240 min) — and asks clarifying questions via AskUserQuestion in batches of 4 (max 6 per run). The ticket's email attachments are mapped to the right task or subtask via AskUserQuestion (one question per attachment by default). After a full preview + confirmation the plugin POSTs the main task (POST /projects/api/v3/tasklists/{id}/tasks.json), POSTs each confirmed subtask (parentTaskId pointing at the main task), uploads attachments via the pending-file flow and attaches them. The main task is linked back to the Desk ticket — when the Projects API exposes a native Desk-link attribute it is used; otherwise the ticket URL is embedded in the description footer. At the end the plugin posts an internal note in the Desk thread (link to the new Projects task + a structured summary of what was prepared: title, AC count, subtasks list, estimate, attachments uploaded, goal) and offers to draft a customer-facing reply — the draft is ALWAYS posted as an internal note for review, NEVER sent to the customer; the plugin never touches the Desk replies endpoint. Reuses the shared API token config at ~/.claude/plugins/data/teamwork-task-wamesk/config.json — Projects token is shared with the rest of the Teamwork plugin family; the Desk token is stored alongside under teamwork.desk_token (Desk uses a separate API key). Never replies to the Desk customer, never moves the Desk ticket on its board, never logs time, never moves tasks on the Projects board, never runs git.
